description_full: Butler National Corporation designs, engineers, manufactures, sells, integrates, installs, repairs, modifies, overhauls, services, and distributes a portfolio of aerostructures, aircraft components, avionics, accessories, subassemblies, and systems. It operates through two segments, Aerospace Products and Professional Services. The Aerospace Products segment designs, manufactures, sales, and services structural modifications, design, integration, and installation of electronic equipment, systems, and technologies, as well as commercial controls, cabling, and defence related articles; and operates repair stations. Its products include aerial surveillance, aerodynamic enhancement, airplane range extension, avcon stability enhancing fins, airplane nose extension, cargo/sensor carrying pods and radomes, fuel system protection devices, navigation / flight display installations, crew work stations, electrical power systems and switching equipment, enlarged aircraft doors, powered airplane sensor lifts, and specialized cabling and harnesses products; and provisions to allow carrying of external stores. The company also provides modifications on aerial photograph capabilities, aerodynamic improvements, avionics systems, cargo or expanded-sized doors, search and rescue, airborne research capability, extended range fuel tanks, radar systems, intelligence surveillance reconnaissance, special mission modifications, target towing capability, and electrical systems integration; and cabling, electronic control systems, hangfire override modules, test equipment, and gun control units. The Professional Services segment manages a gaming, dining, and entertainment facility. It serves owners and operators of private, commercial, business and government aircraft; and commercial weapon manufacturers and suppliers in North America, Europe, Asia, Australia, and internationally. Butler National Corporation was incorporated in 1960 and is headquartered in New Century, Kansas.

financial_summary: Butler National Corp. is a small-cap industrials business with a $335M market cap on $98M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 8% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $19M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.18× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 35% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

news_headlines.title: Zeff Capital, LP Sells Over 50,000 Shares of Butler National Corp (OTC: BUKS) in Three Days

sect: Its 29% operating margin runs 20pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.61x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+26.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 98% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 1% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 45% and a beta of 0.63, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.14 vs 5y 0.40), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $345K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 49% in the 2020 crash, 36% in the 2022 bear market and 75% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 40% below its DCF fair value of $8.79, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 4%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $6.04 to $13.12 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 14.6 vs 24.1, EV/EBITDA 8.5 vs 13.4 and P/FCF 17.4 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 36% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 5.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 8.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 1.2% annual cash-flow growth, 9pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 7.7%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.60).
It converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.18x.
ROE of 27% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 15pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 1.5% of revenue on R&D and 0.2% on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $5.7M (2% of market cap).
Its debt comes due soon (maturity wall about 1.4 years out), so refinancing terms matter.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.2% over 3 years, 9.8% over 5 years and 8.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 59% of profits supports about 7.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 24.4% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 6.7% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own 35.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 14%.
Insider trading is two-way: 12 purchases and 7 sales over the past year, net $140K sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.6% (1.6% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 3.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 348 employees, each generates about $282K of revenue, 0.8x the Industrials median, and revenue has grown 4.3% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $55K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $411K (1x revenue per employee).
